analysis.title: USD Rates Chart Pack: Futures Positions & Curve Analysis
key_insights: CFTC Commitment of Traders data shows non-commercial net positions in Treasury futures are net short across every contract: TU -856.8K, FV -1,074.1K, TY -964.3K, UXY -149.3K, US -68.4K, WN -375.2K.

By trader type as of 10/20/2026, asset managers are net long in the 2Y (+849.4K), 5Y (+2,925.4K), 10Y (+2,928.1K) and Ultra-10Y (+1,723.6K) futures. Leveraged accounts are net short in those same contracts (2Y -804.8K, 5Y -2,107.2K, 10Y -2,117.5K, Ultra-10Y -1,285.5K).
Dealers are net short in all six Treasury futures contracts shown (for example 5Y -682.2K and 10Y -850.5K).
The positioning pattern is a long cash-futures basis structure: asset managers long and leveraged accounts short in matching size. The report does not state this explicitly.
3M SOFR non-commercial net position is -2,415.3K. By trader type, dealers hold +2,628.8K and leveraged accounts -2,373.0K, so the dealer and leveraged books are nearly mirror images.
Swap curve spreads flattened between 10/19 and 10/23/2026: 2s10s went from 11.8 to 6.1, 2s30s from 21.0 to 14.1, and 2s5s from 2.6 to -1.1 (inverted on 10/23).
Treasury curve spreads also flattened over the same days: 2s10s from 36.6 to 30.5 and 2s30s from 70.3 to 63.1. Long-end 10s30s eased from 33.7 to 32.6.
Treasury curve levels sit well below long-run averages: 2s30s is 63.1 vs an average of 90.40, and 2s10s is 30.5 vs an average of 56.87.
The report also charts the 10Y US-Japan and US-Germany spreads, SOFR futures open interest and Fed SOMA holdings, but the text gives no readings for them.
risk_factors: Extreme futures positioning and extreme curve curvature may lead to near-term rate or curve changes.
